### 2026-11-08: # SMART MOOD LIGHT

**2.47h**

# SMART MOOD LIGHT
This week, I want to make a smart mood light that automaticaly changes light level based on the light in the room using a photo detector. I wanted to focus on the asthetic component the most so I started with this as inspo.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CSRBTfO1gnf3OnVHBGadYvTR5GkJjHAY/833c85984d05bc7fe4b6b50b4e5dcc8112bfc48b4e09917829f84ad42b611bbd.png)

I wanted to use a irregular shape, so I went a little and too much and made it too big which you will see was an issue.

# First Designs

I went with a almost a ruler in height length, and my plan ws to use 8001 resin to make the light pass through. But after checking the price, it was WAY over my budget, so I had to tone it down alot.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CSRBTfO1gnf3OnVHBGadYvTR5GkJjHAY/bba8af4784918509841a357c2e4775b40ab6bab8675015532d0c5c1707f16c4f.png)

# Final design
I went with a sphere , the base connects together with pins, and  there are ridges for the rest of the components.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CSRBTfO1gnf3OnVHBGadYvTR5GkJjHAY/debe8a345f70ae0efddc5f77866085a11c2a7a39dd0ee3bdba84b936d9483d0d.png)

Tomorrow I will add the moutnign holes for the photodetector, the middle post, do the schematic and write the firmware.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/bc112901-c502-4658-80f8-d7c635adc03b/video.mp4)

### 2026-11-08: # Redoing basically everything

**3h**

# Redoing basically everything

So it's the next day, and I hate it. It looks very ugly and boring quite frankly, so I decided to do a different design. So this is what I changed:

* Changed the vase shape into two bulges to keep it looking abstract
* Changed the way the top and bottom base connect so It actually prints properely.
* Found out I need a seperate power supply, so added a hole for more wires

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CSRBTfO1gnf3OnVHBGadYvTR5GkJjHAY/67d2f759464147dd73d39c79af7b4dd6f2d4620cfc822dc7faa716a1a93952ec.png)

Okay now that we got that out of the way.. let's get working on the schematic!

# The Schematic

I am using a XIAO ESP32 S3, a photodetector, an adressable led strip, all powered by a phone block with a modified USB C cable.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CSRBTfO1gnf3OnVHBGadYvTR5GkJjHAY/d37978a1544b669605c0a6e0d7e659fdf46ecc98db4f80dd62676ce285a0a49c.png)

Good thing I realized I can't power the LED strip with the ESP32 now before I woud've fried my board. This took a while since I went through a lot of research to get to this point. I decided against making it a PCB, since I don't have the budget for it.

# Firmware time!

This is what took forever! It's mainly because I promised myself I woul duse documentation for ALL of the code. So that was a good idea...

I used the ResponsiveAnalogRead library and the Adafruit NeoPixel library. One to read the PWM values cleareley with added features, and the other one to control the LEDs.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/CSRBTfO1gnf3OnVHBGadYvTR5GkJjHAY/369899fb6c1bca465628f66b902e6053cba83593a077e20e1bf53fc1fef7bc7c.png)
